title: What does LoanDelete do on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced explanation of LoanDelete and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, LoanDelete removes a loan entry when the documented lifecycle conditions allow it. [1]

It is a state cleanup operation, not a general borrower right to erase debt. Repayment, default management and deletion are different actions with different prerequisites. Check the exact LoanID and remaining obligations. A deleted ledger entry should be interpreted together with its validated history rather than presented as evidence that no loan ever existed. [1]

The LoanDelete reference defines the operation-specific fields alongside the shared XRPL transaction fields. Account identifies the submitting account; signing authority, transaction cost and sequence handling still have to satisfy the ledger rules. A submitted transaction or an example in documentation does not establish a successful validated result. Where an amendment is required, confirm it is enabled on the intended network before relying on the feature. [1][2]

Author interpretation: before using LoanDelete, compare the intended change with the current ledger state and keep the transaction hash with the resulting metadata. Treat unresolved outcomes as unresolved; submitting a replacement operation can create a second obligation. These are integration recommendations, not a report of a live test. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
